correctness.rationale: The proof has a compact feasible simplex and strictly convex trace exponential with injective edge-rate Laplacian map, giving unrestricted uniqueness. Symmetry forces two rates. Exact four-block eigenvectors and the budget derivative were checked independently. At each boundary, the derivative sign gives a necessary and sufficient condition by strict convexity, with correct equality inclusion. The equation for matching activation is strictly decreasing in rescaled time, giving exactly one positive threshold when 1<r<2(m-1)/(m-2); the full-price regimes are exhaustive. Limits follow by unique-root bracketing and dominant exponential balance. The standalone checker passed 5289 exact and numerical checks; it does not substitute for proofs.

originality.rationale: The exact same priced-biclique spectrum and critical spectral-gap price are previously known and have been attributed. The final new claim concerns a globally unique full finite-time heat-trace optimizer, both support-switching times, the permanent deletion regime and its distinct activation scales. They do not follow from minimizing a single eigenvalue, an inverse moment, or an optimized discrete-time SLEM. Full-text comparisons include direct matching-biclique prior claims and the seminal 2006/2007 papers. Novelty remains qualified by unindexed or inaccessible equivalent work.
residual_risks: Unindexed specialized diffusion-design theses or different terminology could contain an equivalent finite-horizon support phase diagram.

Known spectral decomposition and general trace convexity significantly simplify the derivation; value depends on the exact all-size threshold and distinct observation-horizon scaling, not novelty of these ingredients.

value.rationale: For a natural family of network interventions, the theorem identifies which entire priced edge class to activate at a finite horizon, a sharp ceiling beyond which waiting never activates a matching, and three provably different large-network scales for delayed activation. The distinct regimes separate budget design under immediate, intermediate, and asymptotically long performance goals. This is an infinite-family support classification with explicit engineering interpretation, not just a generic convex optimization formulation or isolated numerical example.
